f: Level 2 Analytical Application — Theorem 7.2: Injectivity and the Trivial Kernel
f_ar: Level 2 Analytical Application — Theorem 7.2: Injectivity and the Trivial Kernel
b: Let \( T: V \to W \) be a linear transformation. Then \( T \) is injective (one-to-one) if and only if \( \ker(T) = \{ \mathbf{0}_V \} \) (i.e., \( \operatorname{nullity}(T) = 0 \)).
b_ar: Let \( T: V \to W \) be a linear transformation. Then \( T \) is injective (one-to-one) if and only if \( \ker(T) = \{ \mathbf{0}_V \} \) (i.e., \( \operatorname{nullity}(T) = 0 \)).

chEn: Linear Transformations, Matrix Representations & Change of Basis
chAr: التحويلات الخطية والتمثيل المصفوفي وتغيير الأساس
f: Level 2 Analytical Application — Theorem 7.3: The Dimension Theorem for Linear Maps
f_ar: Level 2 Analytical Application — Theorem 7.3: The Dimension Theorem for Linear Maps
b: If \( V \) is a finite-dimensional vector space and \( T: V \to W \) is a linear transformation, then: \[ \dim(\ker T) + \dim(\operatorname{im} T) = \dim(V), \] or equivalently: \[ \operatorname{nullity}(T) + \operatorname{rank}(T) = \dim(V). \]
b_ar: If \( V \) is a finite-dimensional vector space and \( T: V \to W \) is a linear transformation, then: \[ \dim(\ker T) + \dim(\operatorname{im} T) = \dim(V), \] or equivalently: \[ \operatorname{nullity}(T) + \operatorname{rank}(T) = \dim(V). \]

f: Level 1 Foundation — Theorem 8.1: Orthogonal Sets are Linearly Independent
f_ar: Level 1 Foundation — Theorem 8.1: Orthogonal Sets are Linearly Independent
b: If \( \mathcal{S} = \{ \mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_k \} \) is an orthogonal set of nonzero vectors in \( \mathbb{R}^n \), then \( \mathcal{S} \) is linearly independent and therefore forms an orthogonal basis for \( \operatorname{span}(\mathcal{S}) \).
b_ar: If \( \mathcal{S} = \{ \mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_k \} \) is an orthogonal set of nonzero vectors in \( \mathbb{R}^n \), then \( \mathcal{S} \) is linearly independent and therefore forms an orthogonal basis for \( \operatorname{span}(\mathcal{S}) \).
